Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 23-year-old woman who presents for specialized assessment of her lifelong dermatosis and atopic complications.

Her history reveals that cutaneous symptoms began on her second day of life, when she developed widespread, peeling generalized redness. Throughout childhood and into adulthood, she has had chronic eczematous eruptions. On examination today, her antecubital and popliteal fossae demonstrate pronounced lichenified thickening with accentuated cutaneous markings. Over her trunk and limbs, she exhibits widespread polycyclic, erythematous patches bordered by a characteristic double-edged margin of scaling. Additionally, her hair is fragile and brittle; light microscopy of plucked hair shafts demonstrates classic ball-and-socket telescoping defects. 

She also has a significant atopic background, including perennial allergic rhinorrhea with nasal congestion and longstanding asthma that requires an inhaled corticosteroid. Laboratory evaluation is notable for a markedly elevated serum total IgE concentration at 3,850 IU/mL. Other baseline investigations, including a complete blood count, renal panel, and liver chemistry, were completely normal. Her vital signs are unremarkable, and her cardiovascular and chest examinations were clear today. She works as an office administrator, does not drink or smoke, and reports no family history of similar cutaneous conditions.

Given the chronicity and impact of her skin manifestations, I would greatly appreciate your evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Sterling
